limits.value: 45 min of holding (workbook default) unless the wave states it
limits.note: fuel.extra_min of each flight as built by the wave builder

report = scheduled departure - 60 min (assumption); PLT-CREW-DUTY: in-block (landing slot + ROT + taxi-in, or the alternate arrival for a diversion) must be within the duty end. A flight whose earliest possible in-block (minimum over the open runways of the runway-dependent earliest landing + ROT + unimpeded routed taxi to the plan's gate, the scheduled gate for a diversion; replaces v2's ETA + taxi, and far taxi for diversions) is already past the duty end is an unavoidable duty bust (data): reported in the check detail, never a violation. Otherwise the rule fails iff the plan's arrival is past the duty end. Skipped when the departure time is unknown
overtime is allowed (GND-CREW-DUTY reports it, never vetoes) and costs 1.5x in Ground utility; changed from v1 where any overtime was illegal
decision time is T0: a flight landing before T+20 keeps its scheduled gate; the remote stand is exempt (assumption, always staffed)

limits.value: arrivals per runway per rolling 60 min <= max_runway_ops_per_hour / active_runways
limits.note: applied to every real physical runway (strip); fixed queue arrivals count but only wave flights can be vetoed; arrivals only; departures not modelled (relaxation)

limits.value: real runway ids, headings and METAR
limits.note: real runways are used instead of the workbook active_runways count, which is only the divisor of the capacity cap; crosswind/tailwind limits from FAA Order 8400.9 / AFM
not in workbook; spare_gates from workbook remain binding; exempt from gate notice

limits.value: fastest route on the OpenStreetMap taxiway graph, runway exit to the gate's stand; in-block = landing slot + ROT + taxi
limits.note: taxiways, stands, runway exits and holding positions from OSM (ODbL); gates bound to OSM stands (ref, then nearest within 150 m, else a generic stand); 20 kt, 10 kt on taxilanes and turns > 30 deg, +30 s to park (assumptions); exit = first forward exit past the required roll (narrow 1,500 m, wide 2,000 m, x1.15 wet), exits whose taxi network holds no stand skipped; ROT = 2d / (v_td + v_exit), v_exit 25 kt (exit <= 45 deg) or 12 kt; ATC-TAXI-ROUTE fails when no exit of the runway end reaches the stand. Quality gate per wave: every open runway end in OSM reaches >= 80 % of the wave's bound stands, else the wave uses the generic estimate (straight line runway midpoint -> gate x1.4 at 15 kt, generic exit at the required roll and 12 kt; assumption). Runways without coordinates keep v2's 6 min near / 10 min far. Remote stand: + 10 min bus. No taxiway closures modelled. The time is UNIMPEDED: no ramp, gate or queue waits (taxi_wait_min = 0 until ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT schedules hold-shorts), so it sits below BTS TAXI_IN (FCFS medians, ROT + taxi vs taxi-in reference: ORD 2.3 / 9.0, MIA 2.5 / 6.0, ATL 5.7 / 12.5, DFW 5.8 / 13.5, DEN 6.4 / 5.5 min); see the taxi validation (Task 27)
open in 2015 but not in today's OSM; taxi uses the straight-line generic estimate

limits.value: 90 m from a crossed runway's centreline
limits.note: taxiing aircraft never wait closer than this to a runway they cross, except at an OSM holding position off the pavement; on the pavement = within 45 m of the centreline
maximum en-route speed reduction a pilot may use to absorb delay
45 min at large hubs, 35 min at medium/small hubs

limits.value: AIM 5-3-8: 200 KIAS <= 6,000 ft, 230 KIAS to 14,000 ft, 265 KIAS above; inbound leg 1.0 min <= 14,000 ft, 1.5 min above; right turns unless published
limits.note: published (CIFP HF/HM/HA) hold geometry where coded, else a standard hold at the STAR fix; turn rate = least bank of 3 deg/s, 30 deg, 25 deg; TAS = IAS x (1 + 0.02 x alt/1000); lap time derived from these; hold_min = laps x lap_min + vector stretch

1,000 ft vertical spacing per FAA JO 7110.65 §4-5-1, first come first served per §2-1-4; the 5-level depth is our assumption; only flights with >= 1 whole lap enter the stack; ATC-HOLD-STACK fails a 6th simultaneous holder and a later entrant leaving while an earlier one still holds

limits.value: workbook holding burn for route extra and holding
limits.note: fuel_kg = (hold_min + route_extra_min) x holding burn (route extra may be negative, never below zero fuel); PLT-FUEL-RESERVE checks hold_min + max(0, route_extra_min) <= extra fuel

limits.value: 280 KIAS above 10,000 ft, 250 below, 210 from the IAF, 170 at the FAF, 140 kt final
limits.note: converted to TAS for route time T_route; METAR headwind applied on final only; the runway-dependent earliest landing is t_entry + SR + GD + T_route(runway) with t_entry = ETA - T_route(FCFS runway)
current procedures (CIFP 2611) flown over 2015 traffic; not for navigation

limits.value: the flow's free parallel ends (segregated), else the arrival runway (mixed mode); earliest expected takeoff
limits.note: fixed ground traffic (real BTS 2015 departures, wheels-off T-30..T+120): mixed mode iff no open runway end parallel to the majority FCFS arrival runway (heading within 10 deg, same direction, another strip) is free of arrivals; then departures share the arrival runway, else every free parallel end is a departure runway. In pushback order each departure is trial-scheduled (hold-short scheduler, crossing waits and queues included) to every candidate and takes the earliest expected takeoff: leaving the holding point, never before WHEELS_OFF, spaced from the strip's other takeoffs (departure takeoff spacing); a schedule that is not ok, or a takeoff inside an already scheduled crossing's window, ranks last; ties to the threshold nearest its (seeded, simulated) stand, then runway id. Pushback = WHEELS_OFF - TAXI_OUT; the departure holds 30 s at the holding point (line-up buffer); takeoff at WHEELS_OFF, later only if taxi waits, takeoff spacing or a scheduled crossing hold it. Known limitation: arrival runways are v2's FCFS choice (queue on the two best-wind ends), so e.g. ATL east flow lands on 08L/08R in this model, whereas real ATL lands on the outboard runways (08L, 09R, 10) and departs from 08R/09L

limits.value: 1 takeoff per minute per runway end
limits.note: a departure's recorded takeoff is the earliest time >= max(WHEELS_OFF, leaving the holding point) that is 1 min from every other takeoff on the strip and outside every scheduled crossing's gap window (the departure waits at the holding point: FCFS, the crosser came first); the runway choice uses the same time. It matches the holding-point throughput of the ground scheduler (30 s node headway + 30 s line-up buffer). Known limitation: with one free departure parallel (ORD in this model) or a busy one (ATL 09L) more departures than 1/min queue, so takeoffs run late (ORD 45 of 160, ATL 108 of 175 on the replays); real 2015 operations used more departure runways
